prose_changes.new: For a century Ethiopia's emperors had been figureheads while regional lords ruled. Then in 1855 a soldier from the provinces took the throne as Tewodros II. His quarrel with Britain ended in 1868, when a British army stormed Magdala and he took his own life. Yohannes IV took the throne a few years later. He settled an argument that had split Ethiopian scholars for two centuries. At the Council of Boru Meda in 1878 he ruled for the Tewahedo teaching on how God and man are united in Christ. He then made it the one teaching of the empire. Menelik II did what no other African ruler managed in that century. At Adwa in 1896 he crushed an invading Italian army and kept his country free.
